sections.title: Fundamentals, Memory Representation & Modern Language Features
sections.md:
- **Primitive vs. Reference Types**:
  - Memory allocation difference: Primitives live on the Stack or inline within Heap objects; Reference types store object references on Stack pointing to Heap instances.
  - Autoboxing/Unboxing: Overhead of `Integer.valueOf()` vs `int`, object header overhead (12 bytes mark/class word + alignment), memory bloat in collections (`ArrayList<Integer>` vs `int[]`).
  - Memory Footprint Calculation: Object alignment (8-byte boundaries), Compressed OOPs (`-XX:+UseCompressedOops`), references taking 4 bytes instead of 8 bytes below 32GB heap.
- **Modern Java Evolution (Java 8 to 21)**:
  - Java 8: Functional Interfaces, Lambda Syntax, Stream API pipelines, `Optional<T>` usage and anti-patterns (`Optional.get()` without `isPresent()`).
  - Java 11: HTTP Client API, `var` local variable type inference, String utilities (`repeat`, `isBlank`, `lines`), nest-based access control.
  - Java 17 (LTS): Sealed classes and interfaces (`sealed`, `permits`), Record classes (`record`), Pattern matching for `instanceof`, Text blocks (`"""`), Switch expressions with yield.
  - Java 21 (LTS): Virtual Threads (`Thread.ofVirtual()`), Structured Concurrency, Scoped Values, Pattern Matching for `switch`, Sequenced Collections (`SequencedCollection`, `SequencedSet`, `SequencedMap`).

sections.title: Deep Dive: Java Collections Framework Internals
sections.md:
- **List Implementations**:
  - `ArrayList`: Dynamic array resizing growth factor (1.5× capacity expansion via `oldCapacity + (oldCapacity >> 1)`), array copy overhead via `System.arraycopy()`.
  - `LinkedList`: Doubly linked node structure, cache-miss penalties due to non-contiguous memory, O(N) random access vs O(1) `ArrayList` indexing.
  - `CopyOnWriteArrayList`: ReentrantLock thread-safety with array copy on write operations, zero-lock reads, ideal for read-heavy thread-safe operations.
- **Map Internals**:
  - `HashMap`: Internal table array of `Node<K,V>`, initial capacity (16), load factor (0.75), bucket index calculation `(n - 1) & hash`.
  - Collision Resolution: Treeification threshold (`TREEIFY_THRESHOLD = 8`), Untreeify threshold (`UNTREEIFY_THRESHOLD = 6`), Min treeify capacity (64). Red-Black Tree search complexity conversion from O(N) to O(log N).
  - `ConcurrentHashMap`: Segmented locking (Java 7) vs Fine-grained node locking using `CAS` (Compare-And-Swap) + `synchronized` on bucket head nodes (Java 8+). `ConcurrentHashMap` prohibits `null` keys or values to avoid ambiguity in concurrent retrieval.
  - `LinkedHashMap`: Double-linked list running through entries maintaining insertion-order or access-order (LRU Cache foundation via `removeEldestEntry()`).
  - `TreeMap`: Red-Black tree self-balancing BST implementation, O(log N) search, insert, delete; requires `Comparable` or `Comparator`.

sections.title: Concurrency, Multithreading & Memory Model
sections.md:
- **Java Memory Model (JMM)**:
  - Happens-Before Relationship: Rules governing instruction reordering across thread boundaries.
  - `volatile` Keyword: Guarantees visibility across CPU caches (flushes memory barriers / bus locks), guarantees load/store ordering, does **not** guarantee atomicity (e.g., `count++` is non-atomic).
- **Locks & Synchronization**:
  - Intrinsic Locks (`synchronized`): Mark word state changes (Biased -> Lightweight -> Heavyweight Monitor locking via OS mutexes).
  - Explicit Locks (`java.util.concurrent.locks`): `ReentrantLock` (fair vs unfair queues), `ReentrantReadWriteLock` (shared read lock, exclusive write lock), `StampedLock` (optimistic read validation to eliminate lock acquisition overhead).
- **Thread Pools & Executors**:
  - `ThreadPoolExecutor` parameters: `corePoolSize`, `maximumPoolSize`, `keepAliveTime`, `workQueue` (`ArrayBlockingQueue`, `LinkedBlockingQueue`, `SynchronousQueue`), `threadFactory`, `RejectedExecutionHandler` (`AbortPolicy`, `CallerRunsPolicy`, `DiscardPolicy`, `DiscardOldestPolicy`).
  - Common Pitfalls: Unbounded `LinkedBlockingQueue` causing `OutOfMemoryError` under high traffic; resource leaks due to unhandled thread exceptions.
- **Java 21 Virtual Threads (Project Loom)**:
  - Carrier Threads vs Virtual Threads: Virtual threads mapped onto OS platform threads by the JVM scheduler.
  - Thread Pinning Hazards: When a virtual thread executes inside a `synchronized` block/method or native code call, locking the underlying carrier thread. Remediation: Replace `synchronized` with `ReentrantLock`.

sections.title: JVM Architecture, Memory Leak Diagnostics & Profiling
sections.md:
- **JVM Memory Regions**:
  - Heap: Young Generation (Eden, Survivor 0, Survivor 1) and Old Generation (Tenured).
  - Non-Heap: Metaspace (native memory for class metadata, replaces PermGen), Thread Stacks (default 1MB per thread `-Xss`), Code Cache (JIT compiled native instructions), Direct Native Memory (NIO `ByteBuffer.allocateDirect`).
- **Garbage Collectors**:
  - Serial / Parallel GC: Throughput-focused collectors utilizing full Stop-The-World (STW) pauses.
  - G1 GC: Region-based collector, target pause time goal (`-XX:MaxGCPauseMillis`), concurrent marking phases, mixed collections.
  - ZGC / Shenandoah: Ultra-low latency collectors performing concurrent compaction with STW pauses < 1 ms regardless of heap size (gigabytes to terabytes).
- **Production Diagnostics & Profiling**:
  - CLI Diagnostic Utilities:
    - `jps -lv` : List running JVM processes with system flags.
    - `jcmd <pid> Thread.print` : Capture thread dump.
    - `jcmd <pid> GC.heap_dump /path/dump.hprof` : Trigger heap dump without process shutdown.
    - `jstat -gcutil <pid> 1000` : Monitor real-time GC statistics and generation utilization every 1 second.
    - `jmap -histo:live <pid>` : Quick object histogram of live objects.
  - Root Cause Triage for `OutOfMemoryError` Types:
    - `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`: Memory leak (unclosed collections, static maps holding references) or insufficient memory allocation (`-Xmx`).
    - `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace`: Dynamic class loading leaks (unbound CGLIB proxies, memory leaks in custom ClassLoaders).
    - `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Unable to create new native thread`: OS process/user limits (`ulimit -u`) reached or stack allocation memory starvation.

sections.title: Servlet Container & Raw JDBC Architecture
sections.md:
- **Servlet Specification**:
  - Servlet Lifecycle: `init()`, `service(ServletRequest, ServletResponse)`, `destroy()`.
  - Servlet Filters: Intercepting requests prior to servlet execution (`doFilter()`), chaining via `FilterChain`. Thread safety warning: Servlets and Filters are singletons shared across requests—do not store request state in instance variables.
- **Low-Level JDBC & Connection Pooling**:
  - JDBC Abstraction: `DriverManager`, `Connection`, `PreparedStatement` (pre-compiled binary SQL protecting against SQL injection), `ResultSet`.
  - Connection Pool Internals (HikariCP):
    - Key metrics & tuning: `maximumPoolSize`, `minimumIdle`, `connectionTimeout`, `idleTimeout`, `maxLifetime`, `leakDetectionThreshold`.
    - Connection Pool Exhaustion Debugging: Identifying unclosed connections, thread state blocked on `HikariPool.getConnection()`.

sections.title: ORM & Hibernate Core Mechanics
sections.md:
- **Entity Lifecycle States**:
  - Transient: Object instantiated in Java, not associated with Session, no primary key in DB.
  - Persistent (Managed): Object attached to active Session, monitored for Dirty Checking.
  - Detached: Session closed or entity cleared (`session.evict()`); changes not automatically tracked.
  - Removed: Entity scheduled for deletion upon session flush.
- **Mapping & Fetching Strategies**:
  - Relationships: `@OneToOne`, `@OneToMany`, `@ManyToOne`, `@ManyToMany`.
  - Cascade Types: `CascadeType.PERSIST`, `MERGE`, `REMOVE`, `REFRESH`, `DETACH`, `ALL`.
  - Fetch Types: `FetchType.LAZY` (Proxy objects instantiated via ByteBuddy/CGLIB) vs `FetchType.EAGER` (Immediate load). Rule: Default all relationships to `LAZY` to avoid accidental N+1 queries.

sections.title: Production ORM Performance Tuning
sections.md:
- **The N+1 Select Problem**:
  - Cause: Fetching 1 parent entity query followed by N individual queries for lazy/eager child associations during collection iteration.
  - Detection: Hibernate SQL logging (`spring.jpa.show-sql=true`), Vlad Mihalcea’s `db-util` query inspector.
  - Resolution Strategies:
    1. JPQL `JOIN FETCH p.children`
    2. JPA `@EntityGraph(attributePaths = {"children"})`
    3. Hibernate Batch Fetching: `@BatchSize(size = 25)` or `hibernate.default_batch_fetch_size=25`.
- **First & Second Level Caching**:
  - First-Level Cache: Session-scoped cache (default, non-configurable).
  - Second-Level Cache: SessionFactory-scoped cache across sessions using providers like Redisson or Ehcache. `@Cacheable`, `@Cache(usage = CacheConcurrencyStrategy.READ_WRITE)`.
- **Dangers of LazyInitializationException**:
  - Occurs when accessing a `LAZY` loaded association outside an active Hibernate session/transaction.
  - Anti-pattern resolution: `enable_lazy_load_no_trans=true` (creates a new database connection for every lazy fetch, blowing out connection pools). Correct fix: Use DTO projections or explicit fetch joins.

sections.title: Spring Core Framework & Dependency Injection
sections.md:
- **IoC Container Internals**:
  - `BeanFactory` vs `ApplicationContext` (`AnnotationConfigApplicationContext`, `WebApplicationContext`).
  - Bean Definition Reading, Bean Definition Registry, Metadata compilation.
- **Bean Lifecycle Phases**:
  1. Instantiation (Constructor invocation).
  2. Dependency Population (Setter/Field Injection).
  3. Aware Headers (`BeanNameAware`, `ApplicationContextAware`).
  4. Post-Initialization Pre-Process (`BeanPostProcessor.postProcessBeforeInitialization()`).
  5. Initializing Hooks (`@PostConstruct`, `InitializingBean.afterPropertiesSet()`).
  6. Post-Initialization Post-Process (`BeanPostProcessor.postProcessAfterInitialization()` - Dynamic Proxies created here).
  7. Ready for use.
  8. Destruction (`@PreDestroy`, `DisposableBean.destroy()`).
- **Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP)**:
  - Concepts: Aspect, Join Point, Pointcut, Advice (`@Before`, `@AfterReturning`, `@AfterThrowing`, `@Around`).
  - Spring AOP Mechanisms: JDK Dynamic Proxies (for interfaces) vs CGLIB Bytecode weaving (for concrete classes).
  - Self-Invocation Pitfall: Calling an `@Transactional` or `@Async` method from within the same class bypasses the Spring proxy, rendering the aspect ineffective.

sections.title: Spring Boot Mechanics & External Configuration
sections.md:
- **Auto-Configuration Engine**:
  - `@SpringBootApplication` composite annotation: `@Configuration`, `@EnableAutoConfiguration`, `@ComponentScan`.
  - Condition Evaluations: `@ConditionalOnClass`, `@ConditionalOnMissingBean`, `@ConditionalOnProperty`. Auto-configuration metadata loaded via `META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports`.
- **Actuator & Production Monitoring**:
  - Endpoints: `/actuator/health`, `/actuator/metrics`, `/actuator/prometheus`, `/actuator/env`, `/actuator/heapdump`, `/actuator/threaddump`.
  - Custom Health Indicators (`HealthIndicator`) and custom Micrometer counters/timers.

sections.title: Enterprise Transaction Management
sections.md:
- **Declarative Transactions (`@Transactional`)**:
  - Propagation Behavior:
    - `REQUIRED` (Default: join existing or create new).
    - `REQUIRES_NEW` (Suspend current transaction, open independent new transaction).
    - `MANDATORY` (Must execute within existing transaction, else throw exception).
    - `SUPPORTS`, `NOT_SUPPORTED`, `NEVER`, `NESTED`.
  - Isolation Levels: `READ_UNCOMMITTED`, `READ_COMMITTED`, `REPEATABLE_READ`, `SERIALIZABLE`.
  - Rollback Rules: By default, Spring rolls back **only** for unchecked exceptions (`RuntimeException` and `Error`). Checked exceptions do not trigger rollback unless explicitly specified: `@Transactional(rollbackFor = Exception.class)`.

sections.title: Security Architecture (JWT, OAuth2, RBAC)
sections.md:
- **Spring Security Filter Chain**:
  - `DelegatingFilterProxy` forwarding requests to `FilterChainProxy` containing ordered `SecurityFilterChain` beans.
  - Key Filters: `SecurityContextPersistenceFilter`, `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter`, `BearerTokenAuthenticationFilter`, `ExceptionTranslationFilter`, `FilterSecurityInterceptor`.
- **JWT (JSON Web Tokens)**:
  - Structure: `Header.Payload.Signature`.
  - Stateless Auth Flow: Client requests `/api/auth/login` -> Server validates credentials -> Issues Signed JWT (HMAC-SHA256 or RSA public/private key) -> Client submits header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on subsequent requests.
- **OAuth2 / OIDC**:
  - Authorization Code Flow with PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange).
  - Roles: Resource Owner, Client, Authorization Server, Resource Server.
- **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)**:
  - `@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")`, `@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('SCOPE_read')")`.

sections.title: API Design & Large-Scale Processing
sections.md:
- **RESTful API Standards**:
  - Uniform Resource Identifiers, Standard HTTP Status Codes (200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 500, 503).
  - RFC 7807 `ProblemDetail` specification for structured error payloads.
- **Pagination Approaches**:
  - Offset Pagination (`LIMIT 50 OFFSET 1000000`): Degrades linearly O(N) as offset grows because the database must scan and discard rows.
  - Keyset / Cursor Pagination (`WHERE id > last_seen_id ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT 50`): O(log N) performance utilizing index scans.
- **Streaming & Memory-Safe Processing**:
  - Processing large files without loading into memory: Apache POI `SXSSFWorkbook` (streaming XML for Excel) or OpenCSV streaming iterators.

sections.title: Database Performance & Optimization
sections.md:
- **Indexing Internals**:
  - B-Tree Indexes: Balanced search trees optimized for range queries and equality lookups.
  - Covering Indexes: Query satisfied entirely out of index entries without accessing table heap pages.
- **Query Execution Diagnostics**:
  - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`: Identifying Sequential Scans (Seq Scan), Index Scans, Bitmap Index Scans, Nested Loop Joins, Hash Joins, and High Disk Spills.

sections.title: Distributed Caching & Redis
sections.md:
- **Caching Topologies**:
  - Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading): Application queries cache; on miss, queries DB and populates cache.
  - Cache Invalidation Problems: Cache Stampede / Thundering Herd (multiple parallel requests rebuild cache simultaneously on key expiry). Remediation: Mutex locks or probabilistic early expiration (XFetch algorithm).
- **Redis Operations**:
  - Data Structures: Strings, Hashes, Lists, Sets, Sorted Sets (ZSet), HyperLogLogs.
  - Distributed Locking: Redlock algorithm / Redisson `RLock` implementing lease renewal background threads ("watchdog").

sections.title: Distributed Messaging (Kafka & RabbitMQ)
sections.md:
- **Apache Kafka**:
  - Fundamental Concepts: Topics, Partitions, Consumer Groups, Offsets, Brokers.
  - Ordering Guarantee: Messages are ordered **only** within a single partition.
  - Consumer Lag & Rebalancing: Occurs when consumers take longer to process records than `max.poll.interval.ms`, causing heartbeat timeouts and rebalance storms.
  - Dead Letter Queue (DLQ): Routing unprocessable records after N retries to a separate topic for manual inspection.
- **RabbitMQ**:
  - Broker topology: Publishers -> Exchanges (Direct, Fanout, Topic, Headers) -> Queues -> Consumers.
  - Flow Control: Prefetch count (`basicQos`) to prevent overwhelming consumers with unacknowledged messages.

sections.title: Linux CLI Mastery for On-Call Maintenance Engineers
sections.md:
- **System Resource Diagnostics**:
  - `top` / `htop`: Real-time system monitor (CPU load averages, memory usage).
  - `free -h`: Display total, used, free, and cached system memory.
  - `df -h` / `du -sh *`: Disk space utilization and directory disk consumption triage.
  - `vmstat 1`: virtual memory statistics (r: runnable threads, b: blocked threads, bi/bo: block I/O).
  - `iostat -xz 1`: Detailed disk I/O metrics (%util, await, svctm). High `%util` with high `await` indicates I/O bottlenecks.
- **Network & Socket Diagnostics**:
  - `ss -tulpn` or `netstat -tulpn`: Show listening ports and process IDs.
  - `lsof -i :8080`: Identify process using port 8080.
  - `lsof -p <pid> | wc -l`: Count open file descriptors for a specific process (detecting file descriptor leaks).
  - `curl -v -X POST https://internal-api/endpoint -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key":"val"}'`: Verify HTTP endpoints directly from server.
  - `nc -zv <host> <port>` / `telnet <host> <port>`: Test TCP connection connectivity through firewalls.
- **Log Processing & Text Manipulation**:
  - `tail -100f /var/log/application.log`: Live tailing of application log files.
  - `grep -E "ERROR|Exception" application.log | awk '{print 1, 2, $5}'`: Filtering errors and printing specific columns.
  - `zgrep "OutOfMemoryError" application.log.2026-10-31.gz`: Searching compressed archived logs.
  - `journalctl -u my-service.service -n 200 --no-pager`: Fetching systemd service logs.

sections.title: CI/CD & Deployment Strategies
sections.md:
- **Containerization (Docker & Kubernetes)**:
  - Multi-stage Dockerfiles: Separate build environment from lean distroless/alpine runtime images.
  - Non-Root Execution: Executing containers under custom non-privileged user IDs (`USER 10001`).
  - Kubernetes Health Probes:
    - Liveness Probe: Checks if container is running. Failure triggers container restart.
    - Readiness Probe: Checks if application is ready to accept traffic. Failure removes Pod from Service endpoints.
    - Startup Probe: Protects legacy applications with slow startup times.

antiPatterns.title: Spring AOP Self-Invocation Defect
antiPatterns.why: Calling `@Transactional` or `@Async` methods from within the same class bypasses the Spring AOP proxy wrapper, executing `saveAuditLog` within the caller's existing transaction context without initiating `REQUIRES_NEW`.

antiPatterns.title: Double-Checked Locking Without Volatile
antiPatterns.why: `instance = new CacheManager()` involves 3 steps: allocate memory, initialize object, assign reference to `instance`. Without `volatile`, step 3 can be reordered before step 2, causing another thread to observe a non-null but partially initialized object.

antiPatterns.title: Modifying Collection During Iteration (`ConcurrentModificationException`)
antiPatterns.why: Structural modifications to an ArrayList during active iteration via `for-each` invalidate the iterator's expected `modCount`, raising a `ConcurrentModificationException`.

antiPatterns.title: Swallowing InterruptedException in Concurrency Pipelines
antiPatterns.why: Catching `InterruptedException` clears the thread's interrupted status flag. Higher-level thread pool execution frameworks will miss the shutdown signal, leading to orphaned threads.

antiPatterns.title: Infinite Loop Hazard in Custom `hashCode()` with Mutable Objects
antiPatterns.why: Including mutable collections inside `hashCode()` calculation alters the hash code if items are added to `departments` after insertion into a `HashSet` or `HashMap`. This leaves the entity lost in the wrong hash bucket, causing memory leaks and lookup failures.

antiPatterns.title: Unbounded Thread Pool Instantiation (`Executors.newCachedThreadPool`)
antiPatterns.why: `Executors.newCachedThreadPool()` utilizes a `SynchronousQueue` with an upper bound of `Integer.MAX_VALUE` threads. High concurrent traffic creates thousands of OS platform threads, triggering `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Unable to create new native thread`.

antiPatterns.title: Hibernate N+1 Query in Rest Controller
antiPatterns.why: Accessing lazy `u.getOrders()` inside the stream iteration issues 1 SQL query for every single user row retrieved, causing massive database overhead.

antiPatterns.title: Memory Leak via Unclosed File Resources
antiPatterns.why: If reading throws an `IOException`, streams remain open, exhausting OS file descriptors (`Too many open files`).

antiPatterns.title: Incorrect `@Transactional` Handling for Checked Exceptions
antiPatterns.why: Spring declarative transactions roll back only for unchecked exceptions (`RuntimeException` / `Error`). Throwing checked `PaymentException` commits the transaction.

antiPatterns.title: `SimpleDateFormat` Thread Instability Hazard
antiPatterns.why: `SimpleDateFormat` is internal state mutable and non-thread-safe. Shared concurrent usage yields corrupted parsing outputs or `NumberFormatException`.

antiMatrix.pattern: `repository.findAll().stream().filter(...)`
antiMatrix.cause: Loads entire database table into JVM memory space; causes heap OOM on large datasets.
antiMatrix.fix: Use DB filtering via Spring Data JPA Query methods or Specifications (`WHERE` clause execution).

antiMatrix.pattern: `log.info("User: " + user.toString())`
antiMatrix.cause: String concatenation allocates Heap memory even when `INFO` log level is disabled.
antiMatrix.fix: Use parameterized logging: `log.info("User: {}", user)`.

antiMatrix.pattern: `new String("text")` or String concatenation in loops
antiMatrix.cause: Instantiates redundant Heap objects; defeats String Constant Pool deduplication.
antiMatrix.fix: Use String literals directly or `StringBuilder` for loop operations.

antiMatrix.pattern: Instantiating `new RestTemplate()` inside method calls
antiMatrix.cause: Destroys connection pool reuse; creates socket starvation (`TIME_WAIT` socket leak).
antiMatrix.fix: Declare `RestTemplate` / `WebClient` as a shared singleton Spring Bean with configured pooling.

antiMatrix.pattern: Storing plain-text password strings in `String`
antiMatrix.cause: `String` values persist indefinitely in the JVM heap string pool until GC occurs.
antiMatrix.fix: Store sensitive credentials in `char[]` arrays and clear (`Arrays.fill(pwd, '0')`) after use.

antiMatrix.pattern: Synchronizing on non-final Object or String literals
antiMatrix.cause: String lock pooling synchronizes unrelated components globally, causing thread deadlocks.
antiMatrix.fix: Lock on `private final Object lock = new Object();` or explicit `ReentrantLock`.

antiMatrix.pattern: `@OneToMany(fetch = FetchType.EAGER)`
antiMatrix.cause: Fetches entire downstream entity graph unconditionally, triggering exponential joins and queries.
antiMatrix.fix: Retain default `FetchType.LAZY` and use dynamic fetch joins per query requirements.

antiMatrix.pattern: SQL string concatenation in JDBC (`"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " + id`)
antiMatrix.cause: Direct SQL Injection vulnerability exposing database read/write access.
antiMatrix.fix: Use parametrized queries with `PreparedStatement` or Spring Data JPA parameters.

antiMatrix.pattern: Catching `java.lang.Throwable` or `java.lang.Error`
antiMatrix.cause: Catches non-recoverable JVM internal errors (`OutOfMemoryError`, `StackOverflowError`), destabilizing the process.
antiMatrix.fix: Catch specific application exceptions or `java.lang.Exception`.

antiMatrix.pattern: Missing timeout duration on BlockingQueue `poll()` or `Future.get()`
antiMatrix.cause: Indefinitely hangs worker threads if producers stall or tasks block indefinitely.
antiMatrix.fix: Supply explicit timeout parameters: `future.get(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`.

antiMatrix.pattern: `catch(Exception e) { e.printStackTrace(); }`
antiMatrix.cause: Logs to `System.err`, losing context, trace correlation IDs, and file appender routing.
antiMatrix.fix: Log via SLF4J facade: `log.error("Operation failed", e);`.

antiMatrix.pattern: Long-running transactions around external HTTP calls
antiMatrix.cause: Holds open database connections while waiting for third-party HTTP responses, starving connection pools.
antiMatrix.fix: Execute remote HTTP calls *outside* `@Transactional` boundary methods.

antiMatrix.pattern: Using `System.currentTimeMillis()` for execution timing
antiMatrix.cause: Susceptible to OS wall-clock adjustments (NTP time shifts), leading to negative duration values.
antiMatrix.fix: Measure elapsed execution duration using `System.nanoTime()`.

antiMatrix.pattern: Missing TTL configuration on Redis keys (`redisTemplate.opsForValue().set(key, val)`)
antiMatrix.cause: Fills Redis memory completely over time, causing evicted key loss or OOM crashes.
antiMatrix.fix: Supply explicit expiration TTL parameter settings on write calls.

antiMatrix.pattern: Permitting `/actuator/**` publicly without role restrictions
antiMatrix.cause: Exposes sensitive configuration keys, environment secrets, and thread/heap dump data.
antiMatrix.fix: Restrict Actuator endpoints behind robust authentication (`hasRole('ADMIN')`).

antiMatrix.pattern: Using default `CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(supplier)` without Executor
antiMatrix.cause: Uses shared `ForkJoinPool.commonPool()`, which can starve parallel streams across the application.
antiMatrix.fix: Pass a dedicated custom `Executor` pool instance as second parameter.

antiMatrix.pattern: Creating `new Random()` instance per random generation call
antiMatrix.cause: Repeated initialization yields weak randomness and high allocation overhead.
antiMatrix.fix: Utilize `ThreadLocalRandom.current().nextInt()` for concurrent random generation.

antiMatrix.pattern: Missing `serialVersionUID` on `Serializable` classes
antiMatrix.cause: Slight class structural shifts cause deserialization breakage (`InvalidClassException`).
antiMatrix.fix: Define `private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;`.

antiMatrix.pattern: Updating entities using manual JPQL UPDATE queries inside active sessions
antiMatrix.cause: Bypasses Hibernate 1st-level cache, resulting in stale in-memory entity states.
antiMatrix.fix: Invoke `entityManager.clear()` or add `@Modifying(clearAutomatically = true)`.

antiMatrix.pattern: Calling `Optional.get()` without `isPresent()` check
antiMatrix.cause: Defeats the safety purpose of `Optional`, throwing `NoSuchElementException`.
antiMatrix.fix: Use `optional.orElseThrow(() -> new EntityNotFoundException(...))`.

antiMatrix.pattern: Deserializing polymorphic types without explicit subtype validation
antiMatrix.cause: Enables Remote Code Execution (RCE) via arbitrary class instantiation gadgets.
antiMatrix.fix: Restrict type resolution using safe Jackson polymorphic type validation annotations.

antiMatrix.pattern: Unbounded socket read timeouts (`setSoTimeout(0)`)
antiMatrix.cause: Infinite socket blockages during network drops freeze thread execution permanently.
antiMatrix.fix: Configure realistic timeouts (`setConnectTimeout(3000)`, `setReadTimeout(5000)`).

antiMatrix.pattern: Long synchronous message processing inside `@KafkaListener`
antiMatrix.cause: Exceeds `max.poll.interval.ms`, triggering consumer group rebalances continuously.
antiMatrix.fix: Offload processing to background async workers or commit offsets manually.

antiMatrix.pattern: Using relative file paths (`File f = new File("config.xml")`)
antiMatrix.cause: Fails dynamically depending on server working directory launch context.
antiMatrix.fix: Use absolute classpath resources: `ClassPathResource` or environment properties.

antiMatrix.pattern: Modifying non-atomic shared variables inside parallel streams
antiMatrix.cause: Causes data race conditions and lost updates due to concurrent thread execution.
antiMatrix.fix: Use atomic references (`AtomicInteger`) or collect via thread-safe Collectors.

antiMatrix.pattern: Neglecting to close `ExecutorService` on application shutdown
antiMatrix.cause: Keeps JVM process active indefinitely during deployment restarts.
antiMatrix.fix: Implement graceful shutdown hooks calling `executor.shutdown()` + `awaitTermination()`.

antiMatrix.pattern: Cyclic Bean Dependencies (`ServiceA` depends on `ServiceB` which depends on `ServiceA`)
antiMatrix.cause: Fails application startup initialization sequence.
antiMatrix.fix: Refactor shared functionality into a third service (`ServiceC`) or use setter injection.

antiMatrix.pattern: Missing Circuit Breaker around flaky external HTTP dependencies
antiMatrix.cause: Slow downstream services cause cascading failures by depleting caller thread pools.
antiMatrix.fix: Wrap remote integration calls using Resilience4j `@CircuitBreaker`.

antiMatrix.pattern: Fetching heavy LOB/CLOB columns inside simple list queries
antiMatrix.cause: Exceeds JVM heap limits by streaming megabytes of unused blob binary data.
antiMatrix.fix: Map heavy fields to `LAZY` or use lightweight scalar DTO projections.

antiMatrix.pattern: Tests depending on execution order (`@TestMethodOrder`)
antiMatrix.cause: Leads to non-deterministic, flaky test suite execution in CI/CD build environments.
antiMatrix.fix: Ensure absolute test isolation by resetting state in `@BeforeEach` methods.

antiMatrix.pattern: Storing user state inside Controller instance variables
antiMatrix.cause: Controllers are singletons; storing state leaks data across concurrent user requests.
antiMatrix.fix: Pass request data via parameters or request/session scoped beans.

antiMatrix.pattern: Using system environment variables directly in logic (`System.getenv("API_KEY")`)
antiMatrix.cause: Hampers testability and dynamic configuration reloads.
antiMatrix.fix: Inject properties via Spring `@Value("${api.key}")` or `@ConfigurationProperties`.

antiMatrix.pattern: Setting `-Xms` and `-Xmx` to vastly different values
antiMatrix.cause: Triggers overhead from frequent OS memory re-allocations during traffic spikes.
antiMatrix.fix: Set identical minimum and maximum heap allocations (`-Xms4g -Xmx4g`).

antiMatrix.pattern: Array comparison using `.equals()` instead of `Arrays.equals()`
antiMatrix.cause: Array `.equals()` performs reference identity check, failing value comparisons.
antiMatrix.fix: Use `Arrays.equals(arr1, arr2)` or `Arrays.deepEquals()` for multi-dimensional arrays.

antiMatrix.pattern: Modifying entity collections directly inside getter methods
antiMatrix.cause: Mutates persistent collection tracking, confusing Hibernate dirty checking mechanisms.
antiMatrix.fix: Return unmodifiable wrappers: `Collections.unmodifiableList(this.items)`.

antiMatrix.pattern: Printing raw exception messages containing connection strings in HTTP responses
antiMatrix.cause: Exposes internal infrastructure topology details to external callers (Information Leak).
antiMatrix.fix: Map exceptions cleanly via `@ControllerAdvice` using sanitized standard error representations.

antiMatrix.pattern: Invoking `Thread.stop()` or `Thread.suspend()`
antiMatrix.cause: Unlocks all monitors instantly, leaving shared objects in corrupted states.
antiMatrix.fix: Implement cooperative cancellation flags via `Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted()`.

antiMatrix.pattern: Executing unindexed `COUNT(*)` queries on multi-million row tables
antiMatrix.cause: Triggers full table scans, spiking CPU load and locking DB pages.
antiMatrix.fix: Utilize database metadata stats or dedicated count tracking counters where appropriate.

antiMatrix.pattern: Passing `null` to represent empty collections
antiMatrix.cause: Forces callers to add defensive null checks, increasing `NullPointerException` risks.
antiMatrix.fix: Return `Collections.emptyList()` or `List.of()` instead of `null`.

antiMatrix.pattern: Suppressing GC logging output flags on production servers
antiMatrix.cause: Leaves operators blind to GC pause times during performance degradation incidents.
antiMatrix.fix: Enable GC logging (`-Xlog:gc*:file=/var/log/gc.log:time,uptime:filecount=5,filesize=20M`).

scenarios.title: CPU Utilization Spikes to 100% on Live Tomcat Server
scenarios.question: Production monitoring alerts report that a single Java application instance's CPU usage has hit 100%. Requests are timing out. How do you isolate the root cause?
scenarios.answer:
1. Log into the affected server shell immediately.
2. Identify the target Java process ID: `jps -l` or `ps aux | grep java`. (Assume PID = 14205).
3. Find the specific thread consuming maximum CPU using `top`:
   `top -H -p 14205`
   Note the Thread ID operating at high CPU (e.g., PID 14233). Convert this Thread ID to hexadecimal format: `14233` -> `0x3799`.
4. Generate a thread dump using `jcmd`:
   `jcmd 14205 Thread.print > /tmp/thread_dump.txt`
5. Search for the hex Thread ID within the thread dump file:
   `grep -A 30 "nid=0x3799" /tmp/thread_dump.txt`
6. Analyze the stack trace:
   - If stuck in `java.util.HashMap.get()`, it indicates a legacy non-thread-safe map experiencing infinite looping during concurrent rehash.
   - If stuck in application business logic loops, inspect code conditions for missing loop termination triggers.

scenarios.title: Memory Leak Triage (`java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`)
scenarios.question: An application crashes every 48 hours with `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`. Restarting fixes it temporarily. How do you locate the leaking objects?
scenarios.answer:
1. Ensure the JVM is configured with automatic heap dumping on OOM:
   `-XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError -XX:HeapDumpPath=/var/log/heap_dump.hprof`
2. If the application is currently degrading near full heap capacity prior to crashing, trigger a live dump manually:
   `jcmd <pid> GC.heap_dump /tmp/manual_heap_dump.hprof`
3. Download the `.hprof` file and open it in Eclipse Memory Analyzer Tool (MAT) or JProfiler.
4. Run the **Leak Suspects Report**.
5. Inspect the **Dominator Tree** to identify objects retaining high retained heap sizes.
6. Common culprit patterns:
   - Static `Collection` classes (e.g., in-memory cache maps missing eviction TTLs).
   - Unclosed `ThreadLocal` variables retaining large request contexts on pooled threads.
   - Long-lived event listeners missing unregistration hooks.

scenarios.title: Connection Pool Exhaustion (`HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available`)
scenarios.question: Application logs show `Exception: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms`. Database CPU is only at 10%. How do you diagnose and fix this?
scenarios.answer:
1. Cause Verification: Database CPU is low, meaning the DB is not overloaded. The issue lies within application-side connection checkout leaks.
2. Enable HikariCP leak detection logging temporarily:
   `spring.datasource.hikari.leak-detection-threshold=5000` (Logs warning if connection is checked out for >5 seconds).
3. Inspect thread dumps while the application is locked:
   `grep -A 10 "HikariPool.getConnection" /tmp/thread_dump.txt`
4. Typical Maintenance Finding: A method queries the DB, then makes an external synchronous HTTP web service call *while keeping the DB transaction open*. The HTTP call stalls, holding onto the database connection indefinitely and exhausting the pool.
5. Fix: Refactor code to complete remote API integration *prior* to opening database transactions.

scenarios.title: Investigating Transient Database Deadlocks
scenarios.question: PostgreSQL logs report `ERROR: deadlock detected` during high-throughput order processing. How do you resolve this at the DB and Spring application layers?
scenarios.answer:
1. Extract deadlock traces from PostgreSQL logs to identify the competing transaction SQL statements and lock resources:
   `LOG: deadlock detected ... Process 2101 waits for ShareLock on transaction 88102; Process 88102 waits for ExclusiveLock on tuple...`
2. Cause Analysis: Transaction A updates Table X then Table Y; concurrently Transaction B updates Table Y then Table X.
3. Remediation Actions:
   - **Enforce Strict Resource Ordering**: Ensure all service transactions acquire locks/updates in identical entity order (e.g., sort IDs prior to executing updates).
   - **Add Retry Logic**: Annotate Spring service methods with Spring Retry:
     `@Retryable(retryFor = {CannotAcquireLockException.class}, maxAttempts = 3, backoff = @Backoff(delay = 100))`

scenarios.title: Microservice Memory Starvation in Kubernetes (OOMKilled)
scenarios.question: A Spring Boot Pod in Kubernetes is repeatedly killed with status `OOMKilled` (exit code 137). However, no `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError` appears in application logs. Why?
scenarios.answer:
1. Cause Identification: `OOMKilled` (Exit Code 137) means the Linux Kernel OS killer terminated the container process because total container native memory exceeded Kubernetes `resources.limits.memory`. JVM Heap was fine, but off-heap/native memory overflowed container bounds.
2. Root Causes:
   - Misconfigured `-Xmx`: JVM Heap was assigned 2GB, but container limit was set to 2GB. Non-heap memory (Metaspace, thread stacks, Direct ByteBuffers, C-runtime allocations) pushed total memory usage over 2GB.
3. Fix Strategy:
   - Align memory container limits correctly: Set `-Xmx` to 70-75% of total container resource limit.
   - Container setting: `resources.limits.memory: 4Gi`
   - JVM Flags setting: `-Xms3g -Xmx3g -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=512m`

scenarios.title: Debugging Unintended Cache Stampede / Thundering Herd
scenarios.question: When a high-traffic Redis cache key expires (e.g., homepage configuration), database CPU spikes to 100% instantly for 5 seconds. How do you prevent this?
scenarios.answer:
1. Cause: Thousands of concurrent requests receive a cache miss simultaneously when the key expires, all executing the underlying heavy DB query in parallel.
2. Fix Options:
   - **Mutex Locking (Redisson)**: Acquire a distributed lock on cache miss; only the lock winner queries the DB and populates Redis, while others wait/retry.
   - **Soft Expiry / Background Refresh**: Store payload with an embedded logical timestamp field. When close to expiry, a background thread asynchronously refreshes the cache while serving slightly stale data to incoming requests.

scenarios.title: Thread Contention & Lock Bottlenecks
scenarios.question: High traffic performance degrades drastically. Thread dumps show 150 threads in `BLOCKED` state waiting on `0x000000076c112288`. How do you resolve this?
scenarios.answer:
1. Inspect thread dump details:
   ```text
   "http-nio-8080-exec-45" #112 daemon prio=5 os_prio=0 tid=0x00007f WAITING
   java.lang.Thread.State: BLOCKED (on object monitor)
   at com.legacy.service.SecurityTokenGenerator.generateToken(SecurityTokenGenerator.java:42)
   - waiting to lock <0x000000076c112288> (a java.lang.Class for com.legacy.service.SecurityTokenGenerator)
   ```
2. Identify lock holder thread: Search dump for `locked <0x000000076c112288>`.
3. Root Cause: Method `generateToken()` uses `synchronized static`, forcing all HTTP request threads to pass through a single bottleneck.
4. Remediation: Replace class-level synchronized block with non-blocking concurrency constructs (`ThreadLocalRandom`, `java.util.concurrent.atomic`, or fine-grained locks).

scenarios.title: Kafka Consumer Group Rebalance Storms
scenarios.question: A Spring Kafka service continuously leaves and rejoins its consumer group, resulting in stalled message consumption. Logs report `CommitFailedException`.
scenarios.answer:
1. Cause: The consumer takes longer to process a batch of records than configured in `max.poll.interval.ms`. Kafka broker assumes the consumer is dead, revokes its partitions, and triggers a consumer group rebalance.
2. Fix Strategy:
   - Increase processing capacity by processing messages asynchronously using a worker thread pool.
   - Reduce batch intake size: `max.poll.records=50` (down from default 500).
   - Increase processing timeout threshold: `max.poll.interval.ms=600000` (10 minutes).

scenarios.title: Cascading Failure Due to Downstream Service Outage
scenarios.question: External payment gateway latency spikes from 200ms to 30 seconds. As a result, your primary e-commerce backend stops responding to all user requests. How do you decouple the failure?
scenarios.answer:
1. Root Cause: Request threads calling the slow payment API block for 30s, exhausting Tomcat’s thread pool (`max-threads=200`), starving unrelated endpoints like `/catalog` or `/health`.
2. Remediation Strategy:
   - Wrap remote REST calls inside Resilience4j `@CircuitBreaker` and `@TimeLimiter`.
   - Configure call timeouts aggressively (`readTimeout = 3000ms`).
   - Define fallback behavior returning a degraded response or queuing requests for async execution.

scenarios.title: Silent Transaction Rollbacks (`UnexpectedRollbackException`)
scenarios.question: Service execution throws `org.springframework.transaction.UnexpectedRollbackException: Transaction rolled back because it has been marked as rollback-only`. Why did this happen?
scenarios.answer:
1. Cause: Method A (`@Transactional`) calls Method B (`@Transactional`). Method B throws a `RuntimeException`, catching it internally in a try-catch block in Method A.
2. Mechanics: Even though Method A caught the exception, Method B's transaction aspect marked the global physical transaction as `rollback-only`. When Method A attempts to commit, the transaction manager enforces a rollback and throws `UnexpectedRollbackException`.
3. Fix: If Method B's failure should be recoverable without aborting the parent transaction, declare Method B with `@Transactional(propagation = Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW)`.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace`
scenarioMatrix.cause: Dynamic proxy generation leak or ClassLoader failure.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Increase `-XX:MaxMetaspaceSize`; profile ClassLoaders via MAT to locate un-garbage-collected dynamic classes.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: Log disk space at 100% capacity (`No space left on device`).
scenarioMatrix.cause: Logback/Log4j rotation failed or application writing uncontrolled error loops.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Execute `truncate -s 0 application.log`; configure `logrotate` / max history file caps.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: Latency spikes occurring precisely every 5 minutes.
scenarioMatrix.cause: Full Garbage Collection STW pauses executing via Parallel/G1 GC.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Switch to low-latency GC (`ZGC` or `Shenandoah`); tune `-XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=20`.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: `java.lang.StackOverflowError` thrown on specific API call.
scenarioMatrix.cause: Infinite recursion loop in entity tree serialization or deep graph navigation.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Add missing base case termination; break circular JSON serialization using `@JsonIgnore`.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: Redis `OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'`
scenarioMatrix.cause: Missing Redis key eviction policy or unbounded keys without TTLs.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Set Redis `maxmemory-policy volatile-lru` or `allkeys-lru`; audit keys missing TTL settings.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: DB queries hang indefinitely after network drops between App and DB.
scenarioMatrix.cause: JDBC driver missing socket read timeout settings.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Set connection property string: `socketTimeout=10000` & `connectTimeout=3000`.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: `Servlet.service() for servlet thrown exception: OutOfMemoryError: Direct buffer memory`
scenarioMatrix.cause: Netty/NIO allocating memory via `ByteBuffer.allocateDirect` without clearing memory.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Tune JVM flag `-XX:MaxDirectMemorySize=512m`; audit unreleased byte buffers.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: High disk read I/O wait (`%util > 95%` on `iostat`).
scenarioMatrix.cause: Database executing full table scans due to missing or invalidated indexes.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Run `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on active slow queries; create targeted B-Tree indexes.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: Spring Boot application context startup takes >3 minutes.
scenarioMatrix.cause: Heavy component scanning over massive classpath or synchronous initialization in `@PostConstruct`.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Narrow scan base packages; offload heavy setup logic to asynchronous background initializers.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: Socket descriptor leak (`java.net.SocketException: Too many open files`).
scenarioMatrix.cause: Unclosed HTTP clients or unreleased streaming connection resources.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Check open descriptors via `lsof -p <pid>`; ensure clients are wrapped in try-with-resources.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: HTTP 500 error returned due to `LazyInitializationException` during JSON serialization.
scenarioMatrix.cause: Jackson accessing lazy entity properties outside active database transaction session.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Use DTO projections to map required fields within service boundary before returning.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: CPU starvation caused by continuous ForkJoinPool thread creation.
scenarioMatrix.cause: Utilizing `parallelStream()` inside heavy concurrent request handlers.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Replace parallel streams with standard sequential loops or dedicated ThreadPoolExecutors.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: Scheduled tasks (`@Scheduled`) stop executing silently after one failure.
scenarioMatrix.cause: Unhandled `RuntimeException` leaked out of scheduled task method without try-catch protection.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Wrap execution body inside top-level `try-catch(Throwable t)` block inside scheduled method.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: Stale cache reads after database updates.
scenarioMatrix.cause: Cache eviction missing on `@Transactional` failure or non-atomic cache write.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Execute cache evictions using `@CacheEvict(afterCommit = true)` hooks.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: TLS/SSL Handshake failure (`javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: PKIX path building failed`)
scenarioMatrix.cause: Server missing self-signed or internal CA certificate in JVM truststore.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Import certificate using keytool: `keytool -importcert -keystore $JAVA_HOME/lib/security/cacerts`.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: Database queries returning duplicate entity rows in child collections.
scenarioMatrix.cause: Performing `JOIN FETCH` across multiple `@OneToMany` collection associations simultaneously.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Use `Set` instead of `List` for child collections or execute separate query fetch passes.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: High memory usage by `ThreadLocal` variables in Tomcat environment.
scenarioMatrix.cause: ThreadLocal variables not removed before returning pooled thread to pool.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Enforce cleanup in `finally` blocks using `threadLocal.remove()`.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: App server responsive, but health check `/actuator/health` returns HTTP 503.
scenarioMatrix.cause: Custom `HealthIndicator` dependency (e.g., database or queue) failing or timing out.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Configure health indicator timeouts so dependencies do not block health endpoints.

scenarioMatrix.symptom: Microservice instance IP changes cause connection failures.
scenarioMatrix.cause: JVM caching DNS lookups indefinitely (`networkaddress.cache.ttl = -1`).
scenarioMatrix.fix: Configure JVM DNS TTL setting in `security.properties` (`networkaddress.cache.ttl=30`).

scenarioMatrix.symptom: Asynchronous operations (`@Async`) failing silently without logging.
scenarioMatrix.cause: Async methods returning `void` suppress exceptions raised on background threads.
scenarioMatrix.fix: Return `CompletableFuture<T>` from `@Async` methods or implement custom `AsyncUncaughtExceptionHandler`.
